# gh-1934: [GOAL] 413-proof image sessions: compaction evicts image bytes to placeholders (payload-only), 413 auto-recovery ladder (drop→strip→retry), /compact always restores sendability

## Description

**[GOAL] Oversized-image session recovery: compaction evicts image bytes to placeholders (payload-only), persistent 413 auto-recovers via an image-stripped retry ladder, /compact always restores sendability — no permanently bricked sessions**

*(v2 — reformatted per the repo's GOAL discipline; YuryBY's original report is preserved verbatim at the bottom. Prevention shipped in #1920 (closes #1916): `images.maxBytesPerRequest` 8MB budget, history data-URL rewrite, payload-aware stalls. This card is the RECOVERY half — what happens when an oversized payload reaches the provider anyway.)*

## Goal — 413-proof sessions (v2)
One sentence: **a provider rejecting a request for size (413-class) never ends in an unusable session: the harness adapts the payload (drop → shrink → strip images), /compact provably restores sendability, and the original history bytes stay on disk.**
Reproduced shape (original report): `read` of a 2.87MB PNG → 8 inline image blobs in history → `413 Request Entity Too Large` on every later request → `/compact` "succeeds" (158k→60k tokens) → still 413 → only escape is `/new` with total context loss.

## Why it is still broken on main (pinned facts, verified)
1. `overflow.dart` classifies 413/`request_too_large` as CONTEXT-OVERFLOW → triggers compaction. But `compaction.dart` has ZERO image handling (no strip, no placeholder, no eviction) — the thing the overflow path triggers cannot remove the actual payload weight. Token counts drop; bytes don't. This is the structural loop.
2. Registry semantics: an image's FIRST ride is the failing request; retries legitimately re-carry it. No recovery ladder exists after that.
3. #1920's budget prevents NEW oversized sessions but (a) its 8MB default can exceed a provider's real cap (the reported `copilot` provider rejected well below 8MB), and (b) it does nothing for a session that already crossed the line.

## Capability surface
| Piece | Status | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| Per-request image byte budget | SHIPPED (#1920) | unchanged; drop notices name `bytes` reason |
| Read pre-shrink vs request budget | new (tier 2) | `read` on an image larger than the CURRENT remaining request budget uses the existing shrink ladder against that budget (not only the fixed 4.5MB per-image limit) or refuses with a clear tool error |
| Compaction image eviction | new (core) | payload-only rewrite: every image block outside the kept region (and, after a recovery pass, every image block period) becomes text `[image dropped: <label/path>]`; token accounting counts the placeholder; session JSONL bytes untouched |
| 413 auto-recovery ladder | new (core) | on a 413-classified error: pass 1 = drop oldest images until under an adaptive budget (halve on each 413, learn the provider cap per session), retry; pass 2 = strip ALL images to placeholders, retry with the #1889-style latched notice; bounded (≤2 extra passes), never ends the run bricked; if still failing → actionable error (switch provider / lower `images.maxBytesPerRequest`), not silence |
| UI surface | new (core) | recovery passes surface in TUI/line mode (`[images] recovered from 413: dropped N, stripped M`) and in `/images`; headless prints the same notice once (format per #1931) |

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- **AC1 — Recovery fixture (the original repro, synthetic):** fake provider with a 5MB cap; scripted session with 8 inline PNG blocks (tiny synthetic blobs with realistic byte counts); the exact ladder converges: requests stop carrying >5MB, the turn completes, and the assistant answer notes the recovery. (IT-1)
- **AC2 — /compact restores sendability:** after compaction on a poisoned session, the outbound payload contains ZERO image bytes from evicted blocks (byte-count assert on the captured payload), placeholders counted in tokens, session continues. (IT-2)
- **AC3 — History preserved on disk:** the session JSONL is byte-identical before/after recovery and compaction (payload-only rewrite property, same as the registry). (IT-3)
- **AC4 — Bounded ladder, no loops:** at most 2 recovery passes per run; each 413 halves the adaptive budget; a still-failing provider yields ONE actionable error event. No infinite compaction⇄413 cycles. (IT-4)
- **AC5 — Cap learning:** after a 413, the session's effective image budget adapts below the observed cap for subsequent requests (session-scoped; config value still honored when lower). (UT-3, IT-5)
- **AC6 — No-image sessions unaffected:** text-only sessions take neither the ladder nor any notice (REG property; shared suites stay green — red REG blocks merge).
- **AC7 — Placeholders consistent with registry refs (#195 F2):** after recovery/eviction, any remaining `[Image N]` citations degrade to the placeholder note — no silent rebinding of numbers to different bytes.

## Edge / border cases
- **E1** Single image larger than the provider cap → read refuses/shrinks up front (tier-2 piece) or the ladder strips it in pass 2 with notice.
- **E2** Provider cap below the configured 8MB budget → cap learning wins for the session; config error surfaced once.
- **E3** Compaction fails mid-recovery (smol role down) → explicit error with the manual escape (`/new` hint) — still not a silent brick.
- **E4** Resume after recovery → recovered state loads, no re-bricking, budget memory persists for the session.
- **E5** Concurrent steering during recovery passes (#1923 semantics) → mail rides the rebuilt request, recovery unaffected.

## Non-goals
Not re-implementing #1920 (budget/data-URL rewrite/stalls — shipped); no changes to registry ride-once semantics or #1889 notice machinery beyond reusing them; no OCR/transcription of dropped images; no persistent rewriting of session JSONL; headless/line formats unchanged beyond the single recovery notice (#1931); no per-provider hard-coded cap tables (learning is measured, config overrides).

## Open questions
1. Persist the learned provider cap across sessions (config annotation) or session-scope only? (Recommend: session-scoped v1, config annotation later.)
2. Placeholder format: `[image dropped: <name/path>]` — confirm wording/length (aligned with the existing `[image no longer available]` degrade note).

## References
Original report below; #1920/#1916 (prevention, shipped), `lib/src/overflow.dart` (413→overflow classification), `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` (no image handling today), image registry (#195 F2 degrade semantics), #1889 (latched notices), #1931 (headless single-copy notices).

### Original report (YuryBY, preserved verbatim)
> **Summary:** When the `read` tool opens a large image (here a 2.87 MB PNG phone screenshot, 1080x2280), the provider rejects the next request with `413: Request Entity Too Large`. The turn ends with an error and **the session never recovers**: every later request (even plain text) returns 413 again, and `/compact` does not fix it. The only way out is a new session, which loses all context.
> **Environment:** fa 1.0.656 (first observed on 1.0.630), macOS, TUI; Provider: `copilot-YuryBY` (GitHub Copilot API), model `gemini-3.8-flash`; Session id: `01a17da5-1433-7fd4-b108-a458fbb3904d`.
> **Reproduction (observed 2026-10-27):** 1. Agent runs `adb shell screencap -p /sdcard/home.png && adb pull ... /tmp/phone_home.png` (2,865,681 bytes, 1080x2280 PNG). 2. Agent calls `read /tmp/phone_home.png` (tool ends `error=false`, 22:36:09). 3. Next request fails: `error: 413: Request Entity Too Large`. `run end` at 22:36:11 (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`). 4. User runs `/compact`: context 158,861 -> 60,874 tokens (6%), compaction succeeds. 5. Any plain-text message: `error: 413` again (checked 23:12).
> **Evidence:** Session JSONL ~29 MB, 8 inline `"mimeType":"image/png"` blobs retained after `/compact`, so the request body stays above the provider limit. `fa.log`: `tool end name=read error=false` -> `turn end stop=toolUse` -> `run end`, no assistant reply.
> **Expected:** 1. `read` downscales/re-encodes to a safe size (or refuses clearly). 2. 413 must not kill the turn silently: retry once with images stripped/downscaled + tell the user. 3. Compaction drops/replaces old image blocks (e.g. `[image dropped: /tmp/phone_home.png]`) so the session recovers.
> **Impact:** High — permanently unusable session, no in-app recovery. Workaround: `/new` (loses context), pre-shrink via `sips -Z 800`.
> **Related:** transient `Connection closed before full header was received` (retried OK) around `/compact` at 23:05.

content.text:
issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  gh-1934 (413-proof sessions): a renumbering boundary in the window
  ALSO evicts every history image block to `[image dropped: <key8>]`
  placeholders (payload-only, JSONL byte-identical) — /compact provably
  restores sendability on a poisoned session; the 413 recovery ladder
  (`agent_loop_image_recovery.dart` + `image_recovery.dart`, bounded at
  2 passes per response, each 413 halving the session's adaptive
  `images.maxBytesPerRequest`) drops the oldest images (pass 1), then
  strips ALL images including the current message (pass 2, latched
  session-wide), carrying the `[images] recovered from 413:` notice +
  model-visible note; classification lives in `image_overflow.dart`
===
### Playbook: an image-heavy session stalls on submit

Symptoms: `connect stall: no response bytes` (attempts 2/3, 3/3),
`abandoned connect attempt … answered late`, `run-idle watchdog replay
of zero-byte request`, a busy row stuck at `Stalled… · submit` — while
the same model works fine in text-only sessions.

1. **`/compact`** — compaction evicts every history image to a
   placeholder (gh-1934), so the next submit carries zero image bytes
   from the folded region.
2. **Lower the image budget** — `images.maxBytesPerRequest` (default
   8MB) in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or via `/settings → Images`; `/images`
   shows what the last request actually sent and dropped.
3. **Check the payload, not the token bar** — the token display counts
   images at a flat heuristic (~120 tokens); a "98% full" session can
   still be re-uploading 20MB per submit.

arguments.content:
### What changed
413-proof image sessions (gh-1934): a provider rejecting a request for size can no longer brick a session. Compaction eviction turns images outside the kept region into payload-only `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders at request-build time, so `/compact` provably restores sendability; a bounded 413 recovery ladder in the agent loop drops the oldest images under a halved adaptive byte budget (pass 1), then strips ALL images to placeholders with a session-wide latch (pass 2), and yields exactly one actionable error if the provider still refuses.

### Key decisions
- Eviction lives in the request build (`rewriteHistoryImages`), scoped to images first seen BEFORE the last renumbering boundary — kept-region images ride on under the normal caps, preserving gh-195 F2's pinned recency/trust semantics (pinned suite untouched-green). Payload-only by construction: session JSONL keeps the bytes, placeholders ride token accounting, resume re-derives eviction from the persisted boundary.
- Classification is a new conservative 413-shape table (`isPayloadTooLargeError` in `image_overflow.dart`) gated on the window carrying images — text-only sessions never engage the ladder; `images.registry: false` disables everything.
- Cap learning is measured, not tabulated: each 413 halves the session-scoped `images.maxBytesPerRequest` (floored at 64KiB — session-scoped v1 per the ticket's open question 1; a lower configured value still wins).
- The strip-all latch (pass 2) is the loop-breaker: once set, later requests carry no image bytes, so neither the ladder nor a compaction⇄413 cycle can re-engage.

- Out of scope this leg (tier 2): `read` pre-shrink against the live request budget; the ladder's pass 2 covers E1's "or" branch (strip).

+import '../image_overflow.dart'
+    show classifyImageCapError, isPayloadTooLargeError;
+import 'image_recovery.dart'
+    show ImagePayloadRecoveryState, ImageRecoveryEvent, imageRecoveryNotice;
+part 'agent_loop_image_recovery.dart';
+    this.imageRecovery,
+  /// gh-1934: the session-scoped 413 image-payload recovery state (the
+  /// learned byte budget, the strip-all latch, the evicted-key latch and
+  /// the armed recovery note). A classified 413 refusal adapts the
+  /// payload through the bounded ladder and every later request build of
+  /// the session rides the recovered state. Hosts own the instance (same
+  /// pattern as [imageCapLatches]); `null` keeps the legacy behavior — a
+  /// 413 surfaces the error turn exactly as before.
+  final ImagePayloadRecoveryState? imageRecovery;
+
+      imageRecovery: imageRecovery,
+  ImagePayloadRecoveryState? recovery,
+    recovery: recovery,
+  // gh-1934: an armed 413 recovery note rides the NEXT request payload as
+  // a trailing user message — the model sees why its images vanished and
+  // the assistant answer can note the recovery (AC1). Payload-only; the
+  // note is one-shot (consumed by this build, re-armed by the next pass).
+  final recoveryNote = recovery?.consumeNote();
+  if (recoveryNote != null) {
+    requestContext = Context(
+      systemPrompt: requestContext.systemPrompt,
+      messages: [...requestContext.messages, UserMessage.text(recoveryNote)],
+      tools: requestContext.tools,
+    );
+  }

content.text:
### What changed
413-proof image sessions (gh-1934): a provider rejecting a request for size can no longer brick a session. Compaction eviction turns images outside the kept region into payload-only `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders at request-build time, so `/compact` provably restores sendability; a bounded 413 recovery ladder in the agent loop drops the oldest images under a halved adaptive byte budget (pass 1), then strips ALL images to placeholders with a session-wide latch (pass 2), and yields exactly one actionable error if the provider still refuses.

### Key decisions
- Eviction lives in the request build (`rewriteHistoryImages`), scoped to images first seen BEFORE the last renumbering boundary — kept-region images ride on under the normal caps, preserving gh-195 F2's pinned recency/trust semantics (pinned suite untouched-green). Payload-only by construction: session JSONL keeps the bytes, placeholders ride token accounting, resume re-derives eviction from the persisted boundary.
- Classification is a new conservative 413-shape table (`isPayloadTooLargeError` in `image_overflow.dart`) gated on the window carrying images — text-only sessions never engage the ladder; `images.registry: false` disables everything.
- Cap learning is measured, not tabulated: each 413 halves the session-scoped `images.maxBytesPerRequest` (floored at 64KiB — session-scoped v1 per the ticket's open question 1; a lower configured value still wins).
- The strip-all latch (pass 2) is the loop-breaker: once set, later requests carry no image bytes, so neither the ladder nor a compaction⇄413 cycle can re-engage.

arguments.content:
### What changed
413-proof image sessions (gh-1934): a provider rejecting a request for size can no longer brick a session. Compaction eviction turns images outside the kept region into payload-only `[image dropped: <key8>]` placeholders at request-build time; a bounded 413 recovery ladder in the agent loop drops the oldest images under a halved adaptive byte budget (pass 1), then strips ALL images to placeholders with a session-wide latch (pass 2), and yields exactly one actionable error if the provider still refuses.

### Key decisions
- Eviction lives in the request build (`rewriteHistoryImages`), scoped to images first seen BEFORE the last renumbering boundary — kept-region images ride on under the normal caps, preserving gh-195 F2's pinned recency/trust semantics (pinned suite untouched-green). Payload-only by construction: session JSONL keeps the bytes, placeholders ride token accounting, resume re-derives eviction from the persisted boundary.
- Classification is a new conservative 413-shape table (`isPayloadTooLargeError` in `image_overflow.dart`) gated on the window carrying images — text-only sessions never engage the ladder; `images.registry: false` disables everything.
- Cap learning is measured, not tabulated: each 413 halves the session-scoped `images.maxBytesPerRequest` (floored at 64KiB — session-scoped v1 per the ticket's open question 1; a lower configured value still wins).
- The strip-all latch (pass 2) is the loop-breaker: once set, later requests carry no image bytes, so neither the ladder nor a compaction⇄413 cycle can re-engage.
- Recovery is never silent: per-pass `[images] recovered from 413: dropped N, stripped M` notice (same string headless + TUI), a model-visible note on the retried request, `ImageDropReason.evicted` in `/images`, and a loop-level `ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent`.
- Out of scope this leg (tier 2): `read` pre-shrink against the live request budget; the ladder's pass 2 covers E1's "or" branch (strip).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/agent/image_recovery_loop_test.dart \
          test/agent/image_recovery_state_test.dart \
          test/agent/image_registry_eviction_test.dart \
          test/agent/image_drop_ux_test.dart test/image_overflow_test.dart
```
ITs: AC1 (5MB-capped provider, 8×~3MB PNGs — ladder converges) · AC2 (pre-boundary flood sends zero image bytes) · AC3 (transcript byte-untouched) · AC4 (≤2 passes, budget 8→4→2MiB, one actionable failure) · AC5 (learned budget binds later requests) · AC6 (text-only/kill-switch unaffected) · AC7 (citations degrade, no rebinding).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[Request build _buildRequestContext] --> RW[rewriteHistoryImages]
  RW -->|"image before last boundary"| EV[evict → placeholder]
  PROV[Provider] -->|"413-class refusal"| CL[isPayloadTooLargeError]
  CL -->|"pass ≤ 2"| LAD[_Image413RecoveryState ladder]
  LAD -->|"halve budget / strip-all latch"| RS[ImagePayloadRecoveryState]
  LAD -->|"pass 3"| ERR[ONE actionable failure + error surfaces]
  LAD -->|"retry"| RW
  RS -->|"[images] recovered from 413 notice"| UI[TUI / headless / /images]
```

</details>
